_about: THE DTYPE SEAM ABI -- the single declaration both lanes are checked against.
Four conventions sit between tinybendygrad/runtime/dtype.c and
tinybendygrad/runtime/dtype.js.  Two of them have already shipped a silent
bug.  A comment did not prevent either: both lanes were written by reading
each other's CODE, which is the thing under dispute.  So this file is not
prose -- abi_gate.py reads it, drives both lanes, and attributes every
disagreement to one of these four ids.
`site` entries are [file, line, token].  The gate checks that the cited line
still contains the token.  That is a DANGLING-POINTER check, not a
behaviour check: it can tell you this document has gone stale, and it can
NOT tell you a lane conforms.  Conformance is measured, in `rows`.
Generated-file sites (`probe.gen.c`, `probe.js`) are the BEND BACKENDS, not
the lanes.  They are cited because two of the four conventions are actually
implemented there and only inherited by the lanes.

c.note: the frame is Term* fs of n = cid_arity(c) slots; ctr_take at :3136 built it

js.note: op.args is a JS array of NATIVE values, passed through with NO conversion

backend._cite: GENERATED FILES ARE CITED BY BODY NAME, NEVER BY file:line. `bend -o` embeds `import "./x.js"` verbatim, so editing a lane moves every probe.js body line: measured here, editing dtype.js moved all of them by exactly +21 (894 -> 915 lines) and changed no convention.

abi.name: flat frame, arity is a property of the CID
statement: A seam receives its arguments as a POSITIONAL frame whose length is
cid_arity(the CID).  `f[i]` is argument i.  An H.I64 argument is ONE
slot, not two -- it is a constructor node that the lane must OPEN.
Arity is declared once, in dtype.bend's signature, and both lanes must
consume exactly that many arguments.

shipped_bug.did: read f[0],f[1] of the ENCLOSING frame, i.e. arg0 + arg1, for a 1-argument seam
shipped_bug.answered: two allocation addresses, which are plausible pointers

predicate: ARITY-2 LIVENESS: the three abi123_fdiv_* rows vary ONLY the second
argument, over three values with three distinct CPython answers.  A lane
that consumed fewer than 2 arguments returns the same answer for all
three.  Three distinct answers is the only passing count.
ARITY-1: abi123_trunc_* is the identity on one record, so any frame
misread -- over or under -- moves it.

abi.name: a record crosses BY FIELD NAME, and the names are hi/lo
statement: An H.I64 crosses the JS boundary as a JS OBJECT carrying its BEND FIELD
NAMES, {hi, lo}.  It never crosses as positional fst/snd.  There is no
name at all on the C side: a record is a constructor node and is opened
POSITIONALLY by ctr_take.  So `p.fst`/`p.snd` and `a[0]`/`a[1]` are BOTH
wrong, in opposite directions, under the same one CID with the same name.
The names are load-bearing because they are the only thing the two
representations share.

L(R) == R          -> ABI-2 and ABI-3 both satisfied on this record
L(R) == swap(R)    -> ABI-3 VIOLATED (hi and lo exchanged)
L(R) neither        -> ABI-2 VIOLATED: the lane is not reading the two
halves of this record at all.  Shipped node
answers ` : ` here, which is the third case.

It adds the OUTBOUND-only plant that this gate could not see: the inbound plant moves 28/30 and the outbound plant 30/30, and the 2 rows only the outbound one moves are floor_mod|-8|4 and cmod|-8|4.

abi.name: pair order: the value is (hi << 32) | lo
statement: The two U32 words of an I64 are ordered HIGH FIRST.  hi is bits 63..32,
lo is bits 31..0.  Both lanes, both directions.

shipped_bug.answered: C and JS agree on (hi<<32|lo) by coincidence
shipped_bug.fixed_at: n/a -- nothing is broken yet, which is exactly why nothing checks it

predicate: Same decision procedure as ABI-2; this is the branch that says SWAPPED.
Every abi123_* row has hi != lo BY CONSTRUCTION, because when hi == lo the
order is unobservable and the row could not fail.  That is a theorem about
the fixture set, not an assumption: the gate prints both words per row.

abi.name: scalar transport: an F32 crosses as its BIT PATTERN
statement: A U32 crosses as itself in both lanes.  An F32 crosses as its 32-bit
PATTERN in C and as its VALUE under node, and each lane must undo that
on the way in and NOT undo it on the way out.  Concretely:
C   : the frame slot IS the pattern.  Read it with (u32)f[i].  Answer a
pattern.  No conversion anywhere.
node: op.args carries the VALUE (bend's JS book emits 1.5, not
0x3FC00000) and f32_show() consumes the raw RESULT as a value, so
the JS lane must answer a VALUE.
So dtype.js is written in two styles at once -- fp8_decode answers a
pattern while dtype_bf16/dtype_fp16 answer a value -- and only one of
them is what the JS backend consumes.

predicate: These are the rows whose declared parameter is F32 or whose answer is F32,
so a disagreement confined to them is an ABI-4 disagreement.  The gate
confines it by PLANT: an ABI-4 plant in one lane must move these rows and
no abi1_*/abi123_* row.
Plant fixture note: the C-side plant reinterprets the pattern as a value
and back.  That is the identity for EVERY pattern, so the gate uses
fp16(1.1), whose pattern 0x3F8CCCCD has nonzero low 8 bits and is
therefore not an exactly-representable f32.  fp16(1.5) cannot move it.

undeclared: Term is u64 (probe.gen.c:171) and a JS number (dtype.js:162 answers Number(...)). Nothing states which parts of a Term are meaningful, or that a U32 argument's upper 32 bits are zero.

dtype.js's own return-style split (ABI-4's second_site) was not localised when this was written; it is now attributed, but only for fp16 and fp8_to. fp8_from and bf16 were not re-examined against the repaired lane.

THE ZERO-DIVISOR BRANCH, CORRECTED: it is ONE row, not five.  `abi.json` said 'both lanes answer 0 where tinygrad's helpers raise ZeroDivisionError', and that is TRUE OF `ceildiv` AND FALSE OF THE OTHER FOUR: tinygrad/helpers.py:74 and :77 guard `cdiv` and `floordiv` with an explicit `if y != 0 else 0`, and `floormod` and `cmod` are derived from them, so they answer 0 or a too.  Only `ceildiv` has no guard and raises.  Measured: ceildiv -> ZeroDivisionError vs node 0:0 and cc 0:0; floor_div 0:0, floor_mod 0:7, cdiv 0:0, cmod 0:7 -- all three AGREE with upstream.  The two lanes AGREE on all five, so no lane-agreement check can see the one that diverges.  1 diverge, 4 agree; counted `diverge`, never `pass`.  Measured by `.agents/slop/jsfix/jsfix_gate.py`.

THE DECLARATION'S OWN POINTERS WENT STALE THE MOMENT THE REPAIR LANDED, AND ALL FOUR STALE CITATIONS WERE INTO A GENERATED FILE.  `bend -o` embeds `import "./x.js"` verbatim, so editing dtype.js moved every probe.js body file:line by exactly +21 (894 -> 915 lines, I64 ctor 467 -> 488, hi32 502 -> 523, op.run 875 -> 896) while changing no convention at all.  `abi.gen.c` did NOT move, because it embeds dtype.c.  So generated bodies are now cited BY NAME (`{file, body, token}`) and `abi_gate.cite_ok` resolves the name; the `file:line` shape is kept only for the two checked-in lane files.
